summary: High tail latency after enabling aggressive KV prefetch + eviction policy with 4-bit quant profile; request safe unwind and preflight checks
description:
Issue summary: After tenant applied an aggressive optimization bundle (enabled KV prefetch=true, eviction_policy=aggressive_ttl, quant_profile=4-bit-fast) around 2026-03-12T09:10Z, they reported persistent tail latencies (95-99p) on text-generation endpoints. This appears to be correlated with cache churn and increased GPU kernel stall time when the quantized path hits cold prefixes.

Impact: Customer-facing latency spikes up to 2.5s tail; sustained error-free throughput decreased ~18% for this tenant. Affects production traffic for a healthcare scheduling product (SLA-sensitive).

Background: NimbusHealth runs on a dedicated pool with pinned capacity. They recently accepted a recommended optimization bundle from the console which combined aggressive KV prefetch (to warm caches), a TTL-driven eviction policy to free memory, and a 4-bit quantization profile to lower token cost. The combination was not validated against this tenant's long-prefix distribution.

Request: Customer is asking for immediate safe unwind steps and preflight checks we can run before reapplying any optimization. They want a staged rollback with low disruption and a checklist to avoid recurrence.

Desired outcome: Restore tail latency to baseline (<300ms p95) and provide a validated preflight that would catch prefetch+eviction+quant incompatibility for similar tenants.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On a dedicated tenant with long prefix workloads, enable KV prefetch=true and set eviction_policy=aggressive_ttl via console for a target model (redwood/gptx-13b-4bit)
2) Apply quant_profile=4-bit-fast and start traffic at baseline TPS for tenant for 30-60 minutes.
3) Observe p95/p99 latency increase and higher GPU stall metrics (kernel_wait_time) and cache miss rate in console traces.
4) Reproduce across two separate client prefixes to confirm distribution-sensitive failure mode.
observed_logs: 2026-03-12T09:23:14Z INFO tenant=nimbus request_id=abc123 kernel_wait_time=312ms cache_miss=true prefix_len=128 model=redwood/gptx-13b-4bit
2026-03-12T09:29:02Z WARN tenant=nimbus eviction=aggressive_ttl freed_shards=6 kv_prefetch=true memory_pressure=0.87
investigation_notes: Support triage 2026-03-12: confirmed config change triggered ~09:10Z. No infra node failures recorded.

SRE hypothesis: aggressive TTL eviction + prefetch is causing repeated large KV loads while quantized kernels incur longer cold-start kernel setup for wide prefixes, creating contention on GPU streams.
Observed that fallback 8-bit model has lower tail but higher average cost; suggests quant path amplifies cold prefix cost.
Cache-layer traces show bursts of full KV shard reads coincident with eviction sweeps (eviction windows align with tenant traffic patterns).
temporary_mitigation: Advised customer to immediately set kv_prefetch=false for the tenant and reduce eviction aggressiveness (eviction_policy=standard_ttl). Applied changes via support console at 2026-03-12T10:05Z. Initial watch showed p95 drop from ~900ms to ~320ms within 5 minutes.
resolution: Workaround applied: kv_prefetch disabled and eviction_policy reverted to standard_ttl. Customer confirmed perceived latency improvement and agreed to a staged re-test. Next steps: produce and run a preflight script that simulates tenant prefix-length distribution against candidate optimization bundles; engineering will add a conservative gating rule to the console to warn when prefetch+aggressive_eviction+<5bit quant is selected together. Engineering follow-up ticket created.
follow_up_actions: 1) ENG: Add console warning/gate for incompatible triads (kv_prefetch + aggressive_eviction + <=4bit quant) - assignee: Diego Morales
2) SRE: Build a preflight validation script and add to support runbooks - due 2026-03-19
3) DOCS: Update optimization docs with best-practice for long-prefix workloads - due 2026-03-22
4) Customer success: schedule a post-change verification call with NimbusHealth for 2026-03-14
